caption:
🏙️ Barcelona, every building standing today by year of construction — 1850 → 2025.

Until 1854 Barcelona was locked inside its medieval walls. Once they fell, Ildefons Cerdà's 1860 grid plan laid out the Eixample, which filled up mostly between 1870 and 1930, Gaudí's Casa Batlló (1906) and Casa Milà (1912) among it. Construction stalled through the Civil War and the hungry 1940s, then exploded in the 1960s as migrants from across Spain arrived: it's the biggest wave on the chart. The 1992 Olympics reopened the city to the sea, and industrial Poblenou became the 22@ district.

📊 Data: Spanish cadastre (Dirección General del Catastro, INSPIRE Buildings). 61% of buildings have an exact recorded year; 32% were recorded with a round year and 7% with the placeholder year 1936: those are spread over nearby years. Port terminals recorded as one giant building are left out. Heights estimated from floor counts, exaggerated.
🌍 Map: OpenStreetMap contributors.
